tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## opentofu
The OpenTofu Registry is a public index of providers, modules, resources, and data sources for OpenTofu and Terraform. 
You can:
- **Search** for providers, modules, resources, and data sources using the `search-opentofu-registry` tool.
- **Get detailed information** about a provider or module using `get-provider-details` or `get-module-details`.
- **Get just the available versions** of a provider or module using `get-provider-versions` or `get-module-versions` (lighter-weight than the full details tools).
- **Retrieve documentation** for a specific resource or data source using `get-resource-docs` or `get-datasource-docs`.

**Tips:**
- Do **not** include prefixes like `terraform-provider-` or `terraform-aws-` in names.
- Use simple search terms (e.g., `aws`, `kubernetes`, `s3`, `database`).
- For resources and data sources, use the short name (e.g., `s3_bucket`, `instance`, `ami`).

This MCP server is designed to work with OpenTofu (A fork of HashiCorp Terraform) and provides access to the OpenTofu Registry.
For more details, use the search and info tools above to explore the registry.

Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer — your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.

## rea
REA provides reverse-engineering tools for local artifacts, native binaries, managed code, browser pages, and runtimes. Use the tool that directly answers the question; discover targets or inspect inventory only when needed. Tool results include inline Evidence and report their coverage and limitations.

## savvy-progress
Tools registered by the savvy-progress plugin through $.tool.register.

# Plan 3 Todos to Confirm

These are the calls I made while writing plan 3 (`2026-10-31-modular-planters-plan-3-jade-and-guide.md`) instead of asking you. Each one says what the plan does now. Mark each one OK or write what you want instead; a changed answer becomes a follow-up task.

## Jade

1. **What the tooltips show.**
   - Core: "Formed: 12 / 24 parts", or "Not formed: <problem>" using the core screen's problem names.
   - Planter block: its status (Growing, Idle, Short on soil, Paused: ...) and "32/64 seeds growing".
   - Left out: the seed's name, the upgraded count, the ME status, stored power and fertilizer. Add any you want.
2. **Jade version.** The mod compiles against Jade 26.1.8 (CurseForge file 8326300, the one Oritech uses). ATM11 and FTB Evolution 2 both run Jade 26.1.12. The plugin API is the same within 26.1, so this should not matter, but I can pin 26.1.12 if you give me its CurseForge file id or want me to look it up.
3. **Jade in dev runs.** Jade is on the dev runtime (`runClient`, GameTests) the way AE2 is, and `-PnoJade` drops it. The alternative is compile-only, so dev runs never have it.

## Guide

4. **No Oracle Index dependency.** The spec says Oracle Index is `compileOnly`, but the guide has no code, so the build doesn't reference Oracle Index at all. Oritech has the same setup and keeps the dependency only for its own code.
5. **Page layout.**
   - `docs/`: Overview, Building Rules, Example Builds, How a Planter Block Grows, Built-in Cloche, AE2 and Applied Flux, Logistics Networks.
   - `content/`: one page per block, in the order core, planter, power, fertilizer, export, ME, frame.
   - The page text is adapted from README.md, which stays the source of truth.
6. **Book metadata.** `wiki/sinytra-wiki.json` has id `modular_planters`, owner `julian-perge`, and no CurseForge or Modrinth project ids yet, since the mod isn't published. Fill them in when it is.
7. **Tags in recipe pages.** Oritech's recipe pages use only item ids, and I haven't confirmed that Oracle Index accepts tags in a recipe slot. So the pages show one item for each tag:
   - `#c:glass_blocks` as glass;
   - `#ae2:interface` as the ME Interface block;
   - `#c:gems/fluix` as a fluix crystal.
   The ME and core pages also say in words that any glass, or either interface, works.
8. **Example build images.** The three builds are rendered from the canvases in `mockups/layouts.html` with a headless browser (Playwright, which downloads Chromium once), not taken as in-game screenshots. The mockup's fourth card, Trellis, is left out because the spec lists three builds. Swap in in-game screenshots later if you want; the file names stay the same.
9. **English only.** No other languages for the lang keys or the pages.

## Process

10. **Branch.** Plan 3 runs on a new branch, `plan-3-jade-and-guide`, cut from `plan-1-working-multiblock`, the way plan 2 did.
11. **Execution and commits.** I recommend subagent-driven execution, and it needs your commit approval for plan 3. The memory note says to ask again before plan 3 commits.
12. **In-game check.** A Jade check is added to NOTES.md: look at a formed core, an unformed core and a growing planter block. Opening the book in Oracle Index is added too: every page loads, the recipes render, and the three images show.

## Carried over from plan 2

13. **Seed traits.** Very High seeds came out of a planter block whose bin showed lower traits. No cause found in the code. Was more than one planter block or ATE planter feeding the same ME network or chest? If not, a single planter block emptying into an empty chest, with a screenshot of its tooltip, would show it.
14. **In-game checks still open:**
    - shift-click with every slot empty;
    - the seed tooltip cap;
    - the full power bar with Applied Flux;
    - a Flux Accessor charging a power block;
    - the planter screen's fertilizer slot on the client.
15. **Merging into `main`.** `plan-1-working-multiblock` (now 136f695) is still unmerged. Merge before plan 3, after it, or later?
16. **Local leftovers.** `gradle.properties` keeps the uncommitted `neo_version` 26.1.2.116 for ATM11, and `.claude/settings.json.graphify-bak` is untracked. Delete the backup?
17. **README fix.** README.md's Applied Flux section still described the old refill rule. I corrected it on 2026-10-31; it is uncommitted. Commit it on its own, or with plan 3's first commit?

# Modular Planters Plan 3: Jade and the Guide Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Add the optional Jade tooltips for the core and the planter block, and the Oracle Index guide book with every page the spec lists.

**Architecture:** The Jade data and lines are built by a Jade-free class (`jade/JadeInfo`) that GameTests can call; thin Jade providers wrap it and are only loaded by Jade. The guide is resources only: MDX pages in a top-level `wiki/` folder in the moddedmc.wiki layout, copied into `assets/oracle_index/books/modular_planters` by `processResources`, and checked by JUnit tests that read the folder and the generated recipe JSON.

**Tech Stack:** NeoForge 26.1.2 (ModDevGradle 2.0.141), Java 25, Jade 26.1 API (`snownee.jade.api`), Oracle Index 2.0.0 book format, JUnit 5 with Gson, NeoForge GameTests.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-28-modular-planters-design.md` (sections "Jade" and "Guide"). Plans 1 and 2 are in the same folder. Decisions made without the owner are listed in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-31-modular-planters-plan-3-todos.md`; the owner confirms them later, and a changed answer becomes a follow-up task.

## Global Constraints

- Platform: NeoForge 26.1.2, Java 25. Mod id `modular_planters`, package `io.github.julianperge.modular_planters`.
- Jade and Oracle Index are optional. The mod has to load and work with either missing. Every GameTest passes with `-PnoJade`.
- Oracle Index needs no code: the guide is resources only, so the build gets no Oracle Index dependency.
- No unicode characters such as em dashes anywhere: code, comments, lang, pages.
- A comment must be necessary (why, cross-file links, intentional absences), a full plain sentence, and complete. Few comments.
- MIT. No code copied from ModularBees. Oritech (`~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/Oritech`) is the working example for the guide setup and the Jade plugin shape.
- ATE's numbers are never hard-coded in code. Pages may quote ATE's defaults as examples, labeled as defaults, the way the README does.
- `README.md` is the source of truth for player-facing rules; guide pages adapt its sections and must not contradict it.
- Never push. Commit only with the owner's approval for plan 3.
- Subagent prompts that explore code include the project rule: run `graphify query "<question>"` before grep or file reads, and run `graphify update .` after code changes.
- Full verification: `./gradlew test`, `./gradlew runGameTestServer`, and the same GameTests with `-PnoAe2`, `-PnoAppliedFlux` and `-PnoJade`.

## Review Focus

1. A server without Jade and a client with it: the client gets empty server data and must show no lines instead of throwing. Pinned in Task 1 (`emptyServerDataShowsNoLines`).
2. A planter block outside a formed multiblock, or whose core was broken: it must show Idle and 0 growing, not stale numbers. Pinned in Task 1 (`unformedPlanterShowsIdle`).
3. A core before its first scan finishes (Waiting for chunks): it must show the problem, not "Formed". Pinned in Task 1 (`coreShowsItsProblemUntilFormed`).
4. A recipe changed in datagen without the guide page: the page would teach the wrong recipe. Pinned in Task 4 (`blockPagesMatchTheirRecipes`).
5. A `_meta.json` entry or `ModAsset` pointing at a missing file: Oracle Index shows a broken page. Pinned in Task 3 (`metaFilesListEveryPageAndNothingElse`, `everyModAssetExists`).

## File Structure

| Path | Responsibility | Task |
|---|---|---|
| `build.gradle` | Jade `compileOnly` and `localRuntime` (dropped by `-PnoJade`); `processResources` copies `wiki/` | 1, 3 |

| `J/jade/MPJadePlugin.java` | `@WailaPlugin` registration | 2 |
| `J/jade/CoreProvider.java`, `J/jade/PlanterProvider.java` | Jade server data and tooltip providers wrapping `JadeInfo` | 2 |
| `J/gametest/JadeTests.java` | GameTests for `JadeInfo` | 1 |
| `J/datagen/MPLang.java` and the generated `en_us.json` | Jade lines and Jade config labels | 1, 2 |
| `wiki/` | The guide book: `sinytra-wiki.json`, `docs/`, `content/`, `assets/` | 3 to 6 |
| `src/test/java/.../wiki/WikiStructureTest.java` | Structure and recipe checks for `wiki/` | 3, 4 |
| `README.md` | Jade and guide sections | 2, 3 |

`J` is `src/main/java/io/github/julianperge/modular_planters`.

### Task 1: Jade data and lines without Jade

**Files:**
- Modify: `build.gradle` (dependencies block)

- Create: `J/gametest/JadeTests.java`; Modify: `J/gametest/MPTestRegistration.java` (add `JadeTests.register(cases);`)

# Modular Planters Plan 3: Jade and the Guide Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Add the optional Jade tooltips for the core and the planter block, and the Oracle Index guide book with every page the spec lists.

**Architecture:** The Jade data and lines are built by a Jade-free class (`jade/JadeInfo`) that GameTests can call; thin Jade providers wrap it and are only loaded by Jade. The guide is resources only: MDX pages in a top-level `wiki/` folder in the moddedmc.wiki layout, copied into `assets/oracle_index/books/modular_planters` by `processResources`, and checked by JUnit tests that read the folder and the generated recipe JSON.

**Tech Stack:** NeoForge 26.1.2 (ModDevGradle 2.0.141), Java 25, Jade 26.1 API (`snownee.jade.api`), Oracle Index 2.0.0 book format, JUnit 5 with Gson, NeoForge GameTests.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-28-modular-planters-design.md` (sections "Jade" and "Guide"). Plans 1 and 2 are in the same folder. - Platform: NeoForge 26.1.2, Java 25. Mod id `modular_planters`, package `io.github.julianperge.modular_planters`.

- No unicode characters such as em dashes anywhere: code, comments, lang, pages.
- A comment must be necessary (why, cross-file links, intentional absences), a full plain sentence, and complete. Few comments.

content.content:
# Modular Planters

A NeoForge addon for Agritech: Evolved (ATE) that replaces many Powered Planters with a few multiblocks. A planter block with N growing seeds produces and draws what N Powered Planters would, and one connection to the core runs the whole multiblock.

It targets Minecraft 26.1.2 and NeoForge 26.1.2.121. ATE 2.2.0 or newer is required. An optional ME block connects a multiblock to an AE2 network, with Applied Flux support. It needs AE2 and does not exist without it.

## Blocks

| Block | Job |
|---|---|
| Core | Forms the multiblock, applies the built-in cloche, opens the core screen, and is the doorway for energy, fertilizer and outputs. It stores nothing itself. |
| Power | Stores energy. Several power blocks pool their storage. Energy goes in but can't be taken out. A broken power block keeps its energy in the dropped item. |
| Fertilizer | 27 slots shared by every planter block. It accepts only ATE fertilizers. |
| Export | 54 slots that hold outputs until something pulls them out. Only the multiblock can insert. Anything can extract. |
| Planter | Grows one seed type, up to 64 seeds. It has a seed slot, a soil slot and two module slots. |
| Frame | Connects parts and does nothing else. |
| ME | Connects the multiblock to an AE2 network. It exists only when AE2 is installed. See AE2 and Applied Flux below. |

Fertilizer and export blocks drop their contents when broken.

### The core as a doorway

While the multiblock is formed, the core exposes two connections:

- Energy inserted into the core goes to the power blocks.
- Items inserted into the core go to the fertilizer blocks, and only fertilizers are accepted. Items extracted from the core come out of the export blocks.

So one Logistics Networks node on the core, or one cable or pipe, runs the whole multiblock. The power, fertilizer and export blocks also expose their own contents directly. While the multiblock is not formed, the core exposes nothing.

### Core screen

The core screen shows the formed state and part count, the reason when the multiblock is not formed, stored power and draw, fertilizer stored, how full the export blocks are, and the ME status. It lists every planter block with its seed, growing count, module coverage, status and position. Each row has an Outline toggle that shows or hides a glowing outline of that block, for you only, and an Open button that opens the planter block's screen remotely. The server checks that you are within 4 blocks of the core and that the planter block belongs to that core's formed multiblock.

## Building rules

- The multiblock is the core plus every part connected to it face to face, directly or through other parts. Diagonal contact does not connect.
- It needs at least one power block, one export block and one planter block. Fertilizer and frame blocks are optional.
- At most 24 parts, not counting the core. Frames count. The cap is in the server config.
- If the connected parts reach a second core, neither core forms. The core screen names the problem block and its position.
- When the shape breaks, planter blocks stop and every block keeps its contents.
- If a connected part is in an unloaded chunk, the multiblock pauses until the chunk loads, and the core screen says so.
- The core can't tell what is in an unloaded chunk, so a multiblock built against the edge of the loaded area also pauses until the next chunk loads, even when no part is in it.

## How a planter block grows

- Growing seeds G is the smaller of the seed count and the soil count. Seeds past that stay idle.
- One module covers one seed. Module 1 covers the first seeds in the bin and module 2 does the same, so seeds fill both modules first.
- Seeds with the same modules and the same seed data grow as a group. Each seed levels on its own, as it would in its own Powered Planter.
- Growth time, power and fertilizer follow ATE's formulas and are read from ATE's live config. Power is drawn each tick for every seed that is still growing. If the power blocks can't cover a planter block's full draw, its seeds stop growing for that tick. Seeds that are already ready still harvest.
- Fertilizer is taken from the first non-empty slot of the fertilizer blocks. Each tick, planter blocks claim it in position order, and each group claims one item for every one of its seeds or nothing. A group without a claim grows and harvests unfertilized that tick. A claim uses up fertilizer only when its group harvests, so the fertilizer stored speeds up only as many seeds as it can pay for. A paused group keeps claiming each tick, the way a paused Powered Planter keeps its own fertilizer, so planter blocks later in the order can run unfertilized while it waits.
- When there is no room in the export blocks, planter blocks wait. Nothing is voided.
- Breaking a block drops everything it holds.
- Picking up the whole seed run and putting it back, or scrolling seeds out and back in one at a time, restarts those seeds' growth. No items are lost.

### Built-in cloche

The core applies a cloche to every planter block. It always works and needs no item. It uses ATE's configured cloche speed and yield bonuses. ATE rounds a 1-item drop at 1.1 yield back to 1, so a cloche does nothing for Mystical Agriculture essence there. The built-in cloche keeps the fraction that rounding throws away and gives one extra item each time it adds up to 1. With the default numbers that is one extra item every tenth harvest.

## Recipes

These are shaped crafting recipes shipped as datapack JSON, so a pack can replace them.

| Block | Pattern | Key |
|---|---|---|
| Frame | `PPP` `PIP` `PPP` | P = ATE Powered Planter, I = block of iron |
| Planter | `FFF` `FIF` `FFF` | F = Frame, I = ATE Infused Farmland |
| Core | `IGI` `GCG` `IDI` | C = ATE Cloche Dome, G = glass (`#c:glass_blocks`), I = block of iron, D = block of diamond |
| Power | `IRI` `RCR` `IRI` | C = ATE Capacitor Tier 3, R = block of redstone, I = block of iron |
| Fertilizer | `IBI` `BSB` `IBI` | S = ATE Fertilizer Spreader, B = bone block, I = block of iron |
| Export | `IHI` `HSH` `IHI` | S = ATE Silo, H = hopper, I = block of iron |
| ME | `IFI` `FXF` `IFI` | X = any ME Interface (`#ae2:interface`), F = fluix crystal (`#c:gems/fluix`), I = block of iron. Exists only when AE2 is installed. |

A planter block costs 8 frames, so 64 Powered Planters plus 8 blocks of iron and one Infused Farmland.

## AE2 and Applied Flux

The mod runs without AE2, Applied Flux, or both. Without AE2 there is no ME block. Without Applied Flux the ME block does not touch power.

### ME block

- A multiblock can have at most one ME block. A second one stops the multiblock from forming. The ME block uses one AE2 channel.
- Harvests go into ME first and whatever ME does not take goes into the export blocks. When ME is offline (no power or no channel), everything goes to the export blocks.
- Every `me_interval` ticks the ME block moves the export blocks' contents into ME and tops the fertilizer blocks up from ME with the fertilizer set in its filter slot.
- Item moves cost AE energy, the same as an ME Interface. The ME block also draws 1 AE/t while idle.
- The core screen shows the ME status: None, Offline, No channel or Online.

### Fertilizer filter

The filter slot is a ghost slot. Click it with a fertilizer to set it, or with an empty hand to clear it. Shift-clicking a fertilizer in your inventory also sets it. No item is used up. Only ATE fertilizers are accepted. The top-up fills free room in the fertilizer blocks even when they hold another fertilizer, and the first fertilizer found is still the one planters use.

### Applied Flux

With Applied Flux installed, the ME block fills the power blocks' free room from ME's FE every tick, before the planter blocks run, so the power blocks stay full. Filling empty power blocks takes up to their whole buffer (4,000,000 RF each by default) out of ME once.

A Flux Accessor placed against the core or a power block also charges it, with or without an ME block.

## Logistics Networks

Logistics Networks is optional and this mod has no code for it. A node on the core works through the core's connections. The node needs an upgrade sized to the multiblock. A node uses its best upgrade for every channel, and these are Logistics Networks' default limits:

| Node upgrade | Energy per tick | Items a second |
|---|---|---|
| None | 2,000 RF | 0.8 |
| Iron | 10,000 RF | 64 |
| Gold | 50,000 RF | 256 |
| Diamond | 250,000 RF | 5,120 |
| Netherite | about 2.1 billion RF | 200,000 |

Example with ATE's default numbers: one full planter block of 64 nickel seeds with 2 MK3 Speed Modules, insanium farmland and the built-in cloche.

- Power: it draws 32,768 RF/t whatever the seeds' traits.
- Items: with seeds that have no traits it puts out about 24 items a second. With seeds maxed in Productive Farming's Growth and Yield it puts out about 320 items a second, which is more than a gold upgrade moves.
- Upgrade needed: a diamond upgrade covers up to 7 such planter blocks, and power is the limit. More than 7 needs a netherite upgrade, or more nodes on the power blocks.

## Server config

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `part_cap` | 24 | Most parts in one multiblock, not counting the core |
| `power_block_buffer` | 4,000,000 | RF each power block holds |
| `me_interval` | 20 | Ticks between ME item moves and fertilizer top-ups (1 to 1200) |

ATE's numbers are never copied into this config. They are read from ATE.

## Jade

### Jade

An optional Jade plugin (my call, the lowest priority in the mod):

- On the core: formed state.
- On a planter block: growing seeds and status.

### JEI

## Guide

The guide is an Oracle Index book, set up the way Oritech does it:

- The pages live in a `wiki/` folder, using the moddedmc.wiki layout.
- `processResources` copies them into `assets/oracle_index/books/modular_planters`.
- Oracle Index is `compileOnly`, so it isn't needed at runtime.

Pages:

- An overview.
- One page per block, with its recipe.

file.content:
A. Raised bed under a cloche

Your centrifuge idea, refined. Corner legs, a 3x3 bed layer, and a 3x3 glass canopy. Fixed shape with 22 slots, and any part fits any slot, like ModularBees.

  • Footprint 3x3, height 3
  • Up to 7 planter blocks (448 seeds)
  • The bed center and canopy center can't be clicked, so they take frame or glass

B. Vertical farm

A 2x2 tower. The core sits on the bottom floor, and you add floors of planter blocks on top, finished with a glass roof. Grows upward one floor at a time.

  • Footprint 2x2, height grows with floors
  • Up to 4 floors above the base (16 slots)
  • Every block has two outside faces, so all of it is clickable

C. Rosette

One block tall. The core is in the center, the IO blocks take the four diagonal corners, and planter blocks grow outward as four arms. From above it reads like a flower or a compass.

  • Flat, so every block's top face is clickable and you can walk on it
  • Each arm is 0 to 4 planter blocks long (up to 16)
  • Arms can differ in length, so it grows one block at a time

content.content:
5:Modular Planters is an addon for Agritech: Evolved (ATE). It lets a player replace dozens or hundreds of ATE Powered Planters with a few multiblocks, while each one produces, draws and costs about what the same number of Powered Planters would.
11:The owner's farm runs about 400 ATE Powered Planters, mostly Mystical Agriculture seeds. 333 of them grow nickel for a reactor fuel line, each with 2 MK3 Speed Modules, insanium farmland and a cloche. Those nickel seeds are maxed in every Productive Farming trait (see "Seed traits"). Every planter needs its own seed, soil, two modules and a Logistics Networks (LN) node on three channels: energy in, fertilizer in, outputs out. Adding capacity means placing and configuring one more planter and one more node each time.
13:The mod collapses this into a few multiblocks. A planter block holding 64 seeds stands in for 64 Powered Planters. One connection to the multiblock's core replaces the per-planter nodes.
17:- A planter block with N growing seeds produces what N Powered Planters with the same seed, soil, modules and fertilizer produce, and draws the same power.
18:- A fully upgraded planter block costs about what 64 upgraded Powered Planters cost.

31:- In game, the mod reads ATE's live config, the same way a Powered Planter does. When a modpack changes ATE's numbers, a planter block still matches that pack's own Powered Planters. ATE's default config is used only for the planning math in these notes and for the tests. Settled on 2026-10-28 in the second session, from what was open question 6.
299:Your nickel seeds are Very High in every trait, which is the maximum. These numbers are calculated from the code and that statement, not measured in game:
306:- **What 333 maxed planters make:** about 84,000 essence a minute, about 16 times what the reactor burns. If the farm in game makes about 5,300 a minute instead, one of these readings is wrong, and the design's per-seed events depend on it.
313:- Oritech copies `wiki/` into `assets/oracle_index/books/oritech` in `processResources`, leaving out `assets/item/**`. Oracle Index is `compileOnly`, so it's optional at runtime.
343:5. Yours to check in game:
349:7. Changed from the design document: with Applied Flux, the ME block fills the power blocks' free room from the network's FE every tick, so they stay full. The first rule, "refill only what was used", never starts from empty power blocks; the second, "refill what the planter blocks asked for the tick before", left the power blocks showing 0 in game. The design document is updated.
350:8. In-game checks for plan 2, run on 2026-10-30 in ATM11 (`~/prismlauncher`) and FTB Evolution 2:
353:   - Found: with every slot empty, shift-clicking modules or seeds showed them in the soil slot first, then moved them to their slot. The client's soil slot accepts anything because recipes live only on the server, the client never moves seeds into the bin itself, and `quickMoveStack` tried the soil slot before the module slots. Fixed: modules are tried first, and only the server moves items into the soil slot. A GameTest covers the server with every slot empty; the client side needs an in-game check.

338

input.message:
## Final review: plan 3 (Jade and guide), 6b54095..73d80df

I reviewed the whole diff in one pass. I also checked it against the plan, the spec's "Jade" and "Guide" sections, the global constraints, the todos doc, README at HEAD, the Oritech reference, the local Oracle Index source (`~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/oracle-index`), ATE's lang file inside the jar the build uses (curse.maven 9155589), `mockups/layouts.html` and the three rendered PNGs. I did not re-run any suites.

### Strengths
- **JadeInfo design.** `JadeInfo` has no Jade imports, and the two providers are thin wrappers around it. Because of that split, the -PnoJade GameTests can cover every tooltip line. A tag missing its `formed` or `status` key returns no lines, so the case "server without Jade, client with it" is handled and has a test (`empty_server_data_shows_no_lines`).
- **Correct by construction.** A core that has not finished its first scan shows "Not formed: Waiting for chunks to load":
  - `CoreBlockEntity.java:37` starts `lastScan` as `WAITING_FOR_CHUNKS`.
  - `ScanResult.formed()` is `problem == NONE`.
  - The part count matches the core screen (`CoreMenu.java:82` uses the same `partCount()`).
- **Planter state.** A planter block that loses its core goes back to IDLE with 0 growing, through the `stopFromCore` and `STALE_TICKS` path. `PlanterLifecycleTests.java:258` already covers this.
- **Plugin shape.** The plugin matches Oritech: `@WailaPlugin`, data providers registered on the block entity classes, components on the block classes, and the uid used for the config label keys.
- **Book layout.** The layout matches Oracle Index's `V1DocsFormat`, which I checked in its source:
  - `/docs`, `/content` and `/assets` are where the book expects them.
  - Schema "1" is read from `sinytra-wiki.json`.
  - `<Callout variant="info">` maps to NOTE.
  - `@modular_planters:x` links resolve through the frontmatter `id`.
  - Unknown item ids are guarded, so the ME page without AE2 renders empty slots and does not crash.
- **WikiStructureTest.** `blockPagesMatchTheirRecipes` compares each page against the generated recipe JSON. That catches recipe drift, the riskiest failure for a guide.
- **Content.** I compared every page against README and found no contradictions; the numbers match. All added text is ASCII. The `.gitignore` anchor to `/docs/` is the minimal correct fix.

### Issues

#### Critical (Must Fix)
None.

#### Important (Should Fix)

1. **The example build images have no color key** (`wiki/docs/example_builds.mdx:5-21`).
   - **What's wrong:** The three PNGs show orange, green, red, brown, blue, purple and gray cubes plus translucent glass, but nothing says what each color means. The mockup has the key (`mockups/layouts.html:22-30`: Core orange, Planter green, Power red, Fertilizer brown, Export blue, ME purple, Frame gray, cloche glass), but it sits outside the canvases, so the screenshots dropped it.
   - **Why it matters:** A player cannot tell which block is the core, power or export, which is the point of showing builds. Two images also show a glass canopy. A player can read that as the glass the built-in cloche needs, but the cloche needs no glass.
   - **Fix:** Add a short key list to `example_builds.mdx`, plus one line saying the glass is decoration and not part of the multiblock.
   - **Plan gap:** Plan Task 6 Step 2 did not ask for a key, so this is a gap in the plan itself.

2. **The in-game checks for Jade and the book are not recorded anywhere.**
   - **What's wrong:** Plan Task 2 Step 4, todo item 12 and the ledger's Task 2 ruling all say the Jade check (formed core, unformed core, growing planter block) and the book check (pages load, recipes render, images show) were moved to NOTES.md. NOTES.md has neither. Its item 9 still says plan 3 is "not started".
   - **Why it matters:** No automated check sees Jade register `MPJadePlugin` or render a tooltip. Jade catches plugin exceptions, so passing GameTests with Jade loaded does not prove registration worked. Nothing has opened the book either. These are the only checks of the user-facing result.
   - **Fix:** The controller adds both checklists to NOTES.md at wrap-up. It is a local, gitignored file, so no commit is involved.

3. **"Powered Planter" is not ATE's name for the block** (`wiki/content/planter.mdx:20`, `wiki/docs/overview.mdx:5`, `wiki/docs/growing.mdx:7`, README throughout).
   - **What's wrong:** The ATE jar the build uses names `agritechevolved:advanced_planter` "Advanced Planter", and "Powered Planter" appears nowhere in ATE's lang file. The guide's frame recipe slot shows "Advanced Planter" on hover, while the planter page says "64 Powered Planters". A player who searches JEI for "Powered Planter" finds nothing. The same drift exists for "MK3 Speed Modules"; ATE's name is "Speed Upgrade MK3".
   - **Status:** This predates plan 3. README is the source of truth and uses the same words, so the ledger's Task 4 note "matches README" is accurate, but nobody checked the name against ATE.
   - **Fix:** This is an owner call. Pack lang overrides are possible. If the owner confirms ATE's names, change README, the spec wording and the guide pages together.

#### Minor (Nice to Have)

1. **The `MPJadePlugin` comment is imprecise** (`jade/MPJadePlugin.java:12`). "Nothing outside this package references these classes" reads as false, because `JadeInfo` is in the same package and `JadeTests` references it. Name the three classes instead: MPJadePlugin, CoreProvider and PlanterProvider.
2. **Server data keys are not namespaced** (`jade/JadeInfo.java:17-20, 37-39`). The keys `formed`, `status`, `growing`, `seeds`, `parts` and `cap` go into Jade's server data tag, which every provider on that block shares. Oritech namespaces its key (`"oritech:controller_name"`). I found no collision in Jade's built-in addons, so the risk is low. The fix is a constant prefix.
3. **The plan's Review Focus 3 overclaims.** It says `core_shows_its_problem_until_formed` pins "a core before its first scan finishes". The test actually breaks a power block after the core forms. The before-first-scan behavior is correct by construction (see Strengths), so this only affects what the plan claims, not the code.
4. **The power page leaves out a qualifier** (`wiki/content/power.mdx:24`). "A Flux Accessor placed against the core or a power block also charges it" is missing "With Applied Flux installed", which README has by placing that sentence under the Applied Flux section.
5. **The part cap is stated as a fixed number** (`wiki/docs/building.mdx:7` and the same README line). "At most 24 parts" ships in the jar, so a pack that changes `part_cap` shows a wrong number. "24 by default" matches how the power page treats `power_block_buffer`. Change README too.
6. **The PNGs include part of the mockup card.** All three show the card's light-gray background and a white rounded strip along the top edge. This is cosmetic in Oracle Index's dark UI. Crop or re-render.
7. **A missing link** (`wiki/docs/example_builds.mdx:23`). "the Building Rules page" could be a `$building` link.

### Triage of the ledger's deferred minors

| Ledger item | Ruling |
|---|---|
| T1: JadeTests import order | Can stay. |
| T1: JadeInfo class comment has a weak why | Can stay. If the MPJadePlugin comment is touched anyway, a sharper version is: "This class imports nothing from Jade, so the GameTests can call it whether or not Jade is installed." |
| T1: core() writes the problem name when formed | Can stay. It is harmless and never read. |
| T1: no RED run recorded | Can stay. This is process only, and the tests exercise real rigs. |
| T2: README Jade section does not name the cap | Can stay. Adding "where cap is the `part_cap` server option" is optional polish. |
| T3: frontmatter checks are exact-line and accept an empty title | Can stay. |
| T3: everyModAssetExists regex fails open | Can stay. All three uses put `location` first. `<ModAsset[^>]*\slocation="..."` would close the gap cheaply. |
| T4: `assertTrue(!x)` and the hard-coded count of 7 | Can stay. The 7 is a useful tripwire when a recipe is added. |
| T4: advanced_planter vs "Powered Planter" | Do not leave this as a minor. It is Important 3 above: ATE's in-game name is "Advanced Planter". It needs an owner decision before merge, and any fix spans README too. |
| T5: extra "See ... block" link lines; ae2 and building pages have no block links | Can stay. |
| T6: images rendered at 1x and shown at width 512 | Can stay. Oritech ships images of the same size (481x381, 501x403) at `width={512}`. |

**Must fix before merge:** Important 1 (color key) and Important 2 (NOTES.md checklist). Important 3 needs the owner's answer. Everything else can stay.

### Declined to judge
- Jade 26.1.8 vs the packs' 26.1.12: todo 2, an owner call.
- Oracle Index not on `compileOnly`, which deviates from the spec: todo 4, deliberate and listed.
- One shown item per tag in the recipe slots: todo 7.
- Rendered mockups instead of in-game screenshots: todo 8.
- English only: todo 9.
- What the tooltips leave out (seed name, power, ME status, and an "N / cap" count on "Too many parts"): todo 1.
- The ME page appearing in the book without AE2: Oracle Index guards unknown ids (`MarkdownParser.java:941,952`) and the page says it needs AE2. The spec is silent and there is no failure mode.
- The branch, merge into main, the carried-over seed-trait repro and local leftovers: todos 10 and 13-16, outside this diff.
- graphify-out graph updates: not in this range, because the controller commits them separately.

### Recommendations

## Final review: plan 3 (Jade and guide), 6b54095..73d80df

I reviewed the whole diff in one pass. I also checked it against the plan, the spec's "Jade" and "Guide" sections, the global constraints, the todos doc, README at HEAD, the Oritech reference, the local Oracle Index source (`~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/oracle-index`), ATE's lang file inside the jar the build uses (curse.maven 9155589), `mockups/layouts.html` and the three rendered PNGs. I did not re-run any suites.

### Strengths
- **JadeInfo design.** `JadeInfo` has no Jade imports, and the two providers are thin wrappers around it. Because of that split, the -PnoJade GameTests can cover every tooltip line. A tag missing its `formed` or `status` key returns no lines, so the case "server without Jade, client with it" is handled and has a test (`empty_server_data_shows_no_lines`).
- **Correct by construction.** A core that has not finished its first scan shows "Not formed: Waiting for chunks to load":
  - `CoreBlockEntity.java:37` starts `lastScan` as `WAITING_FOR_CHUNKS`.
  - `ScanResult.formed()` is `problem == NONE`.
  - The part count matches the core screen (`CoreMenu.java:82` uses the same `partCount()`).
- **Planter state.** A planter block that loses its core goes back to IDLE with 0 growing, through the `stopFromCore` and `STALE_TICKS` path. `PlanterLifecycleTests.java:258` already covers this.
- **Plugin shape.** The plugin matches Oritech: `@WailaPlugin`, data providers registered on the block entity classes, components on the block classes, and the uid used for the config label keys.
- **Book layout.** The layout matches Oracle Index's `V1DocsFormat`, which I checked in its source:
  - `/docs`, `/content` and `/assets` are where the book expects them.
  - Schema "1" is read from `sinytra-wiki.json`.
  - `<Callout variant="info">` maps to NOTE.
  - `@modular_planters:x` links resolve through the frontmatter `id`.
  - Unknown item ids are guarded, so the ME page without AE2 renders empty slots and does not crash.
- **WikiStructureTest.** `blockPagesMatchTheirRecipes` compares each page against the generated recipe JSON. That catches recipe drift, the riskiest failure for a guide.
- **Content.** I compared every page against README and found no contradictions; the numbers match. All added text is ASCII. The `.gitignore` anchor to `/docs/` is the minimal correct fix.

### Issues

#### Critical (Must Fix)
None.

#### Important (Should Fix)

1. **The example build images have no color key** (`wiki/docs/example_builds.mdx:5-21`).
   - **What's wrong:** The three PNGs show orange, green, red, brown, blue, purple and gray cubes plus translucent glass, but nothing says what each color means. The mockup has the key (`mockups/layouts.html:22-30`: Core orange, Planter green, Power red, Fertilizer brown, Export blue, ME purple, Frame gray, cloche glass), but it sits outside the canvases, so the screenshots dropped it.
   - **Why it matters:** A player cannot tell which block is the core, power or export, which is the point of showing builds. Two images also show a glass canopy. A player can read that as the glass the built-in cloche needs, but the cloche needs no glass.
   - **Fix:** Add a short key list to `example_builds.mdx`, plus one line saying the glass is decoration and not part of the multiblock.
   - **Plan gap:** Plan Task 6 Step 2 did not ask for a key, so this is a gap in the plan itself.

2. **The in-game checks for Jade and the book are not recorded anywhere.**
   - **What's wrong:** Plan Task 2 Step 4, todo item 12 and the ledger's Task 2 ruling all say the Jade check (formed core, unformed core, growing planter block) and the book check (pages load, recipes render, images show) were moved to NOTES.md. NOTES.md has neither. Its item 9 still says plan 3 is "not started".
   - **Why it matters:** No automated check sees Jade register `MPJadePlugin` or render a tooltip. Jade catches plugin exceptions, so passing GameTests with Jade loaded does not prove registration worked. Nothing has opened the book either. These are the only checks of the user-facing result.
   - **Fix:** The controller adds both checklists to NOTES.md at wrap-up. It is a local, gitignored file, so no commit is involved.

3. **"Powered Planter" is not ATE's name for the block** (`wiki/content/planter.mdx:20`, `wiki/docs/overview.mdx:5`, `wiki/docs/growing.mdx:7`, README throughout).
   - **What's wrong:** The ATE jar the build uses names `agritechevolved:advanced_planter` "Advanced Planter", and "Powered Planter" appears nowhere in ATE's lang file. The guide's frame recipe slot shows "Advanced Planter" on hover, while the planter page says "64 Powered Planters". A player who searches JEI for "Powered Planter" finds nothing. The same drift exists for "MK3 Speed Modules"; ATE's name is "Speed Upgrade MK3".
   - **Status:** This predates plan 3. README is the source of truth and uses the same words, so the ledger's Task 4 note "matches README" is accurate, but nobody checked the name against ATE.
   - **Fix:** This is an owner call. Pack lang overrides are possible. If the owner confirms ATE's names, change README, the spec wording and the guide pages together.

#### Minor (Nice to Have)

1. **The `MPJadePlugin` comment is imprecise** (`jade/MPJadePlugin.java:12`). "Nothing outside this package references these classes" reads as false, because `JadeInfo` is in the same package and `JadeTests` references it. Name the three classes instead: MPJadePlugin, CoreProvider and PlanterProvider.
2. **Server data keys are not namespaced** (`jade/JadeInfo.java:17-20, 37-39`). The keys `formed`, `status`, `growing`, `seeds`, `parts` and `cap` go into Jade's server data tag, which every provider on that block shares. Oritech namespaces its key (`"oritech:controller_name"`). I found no collision in Jade's built-in addons, so the risk is low. The fix is a constant prefix.
3. **The plan's Review Focus 3 overclaims.** It says `core_shows_its_problem_until_formed` pins "a core before its first scan finishes". The test actually breaks a power block after the core forms. The before-first-scan behavior is correct by construction (see Strengths), so this only affects what the plan claims, not the code.
4. **The power page leaves out a qualifier** (`wiki/content/power.mdx:24`). "A Flux Accessor placed against the core or a power block also charges it" is missing "With Applied Flux installed", which README has by placing that sentence under the Applied Flux section.
5. **The part cap is stated as a fixed number** (`wiki/docs/building.mdx:7` and the same README line). "At most 24 parts" ships in the jar, so a pack that changes `part_cap` shows a wrong number. "24 by default" matches how the power page treats `power_block_buffer`. Change README too.
6. **The PNGs include part of the mockup card.** All three show the card's light-gray background and a white rounded strip along the top edge. This is cosmetic in Oracle Index's dark UI. Crop or re-render.
7. **A missing link** (`wiki/docs/example_builds.mdx:23`). "the Building Rules page" could be a `$building` link.

### Triage of the ledger's deferred minors

| Ledger item | Ruling |
|---|---|
| T1: JadeTests import order | Can stay. |
| T1: JadeInfo class comment has a weak why | Can stay. If the MPJadePlugin comment is touched anyway, a sharper version is: "This class imports nothing from Jade, so the GameTests can call it whether or not Jade is installed." |
| T1: core() writes the problem name when formed | Can stay. It is harmless and never read. |
| T1: no RED run recorded | Can stay. This is process only, and the tests exercise real rigs. |
| T2: README Jade section does not name the cap | Can stay. Adding "where cap is the `part_cap` server option" is optional polish. |
| T3: frontmatter checks are exact-line and accept an empty title | Can stay. |
| T3: everyModAssetExists regex fails open | Can stay. All three uses put `location` first. `<ModAsset[^>]*\slocation="..."` would close the gap cheaply. |
| T4: `assertTrue(!x)` and the hard-coded count of 7 | Can stay. The 7 is a useful tripwire when a recipe is added. |
| T4: advanced_planter vs "Powered Planter" | Do not leave this as a minor. It is Important 3 above: ATE's in-game name is "Advanced Planter". It needs an owner decision before merge, and any fix spans README too. |
| T5: extra "See ... block" link lines; ae2 and building pages have no block links | Can stay. |
| T6: images rendered at 1x and shown at width 512 | Can stay. Oritech ships images of the same size (481x381, 501x403) at `width={512}`. |

**Must fix before merge:** Important 1 (color key) and Important 2 (NOTES.md checklist). Important 3 needs the owner's answer. Everything else can stay.

### Declined to judge

- One shown item per tag in the recipe slots: todo 7.

- The branch, merge into main, the carried-over seed-trait repro and local leftovers: todos 10 and 13-16, outside this diff.

- A one-line plan rule for images: if the source image has a key outside the screenshot area, carry the key into the page.

### Assessment

**Ready to merge?** With fixes.

**Reasoning:** The Jade code and the guide's structure are correct, well tested against real block entities and generated recipes, and match Oracle Index's actual format. The example builds page cannot teach anything without a color key, the in-game checks that are the only check of the user-facing result are not recorded, and the "Powered Planter" name needs the owner's call.
